messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Pagerduty -> fabric-degradation on redwood-serving-prod. Elevated packet retransmits + pod restarts. Page: 1881112222

alex: I'm on it. Alerts show increased mlx5 retransmits on several HCAs, and multiple model-serving pods restarted within the last 8m with CUDA OOMs.

maria: ack. which region? is this single rack or multi-node?

alex: us-west-2 cluster, nodes w/ label gpu-type=a5000. Looks localized to rack-7 fabric switches. Quick snapshot of pod restarts:

```text
kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-server -o wide
model-server-7b9c  CrashLoopBackOff  2/3  192.168.40.12  node-07
model-server-8d3f  Running           1/3  192.168.40.13  node-08
model-server-2a1e  CrashLoopBackOff  1/3  192.168.40.11  node-06
```

alex: and sample from dmesg on node-07:

```text
[ 1023.123456] mlx5_core 0000:3b:00.0: mlx5e: HCA link flapping: tx drops=1200, rx drops=980
[ 1023.125678] nv_peer_mem: failed to pin pages: -110
[ 1023.130001] container model-server[4211]: CUDA OOM: out of memory while allocating 256MB
```

chen (infra): cpu/oom events + HCA drops often mean the RDMA QP timeouts are causing long stalls and the runtime accumulates KV cache + inflight state triggering OOM.

maria: agree. immediate mitigation options: 1) move traffic off affected nodes (drain/cordon) 2) enable TCP fallback routing for model-serving (we have a config knob) 3) reduce max_concurrency & batch_size for the model route to limit memory.

alex: initiating cordon/drain for node-07 and node-06 now, and toggling tcp fallback for the route. Running:

```bash
kubectl cordon node-07
kubectl drain node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
rdctl route update --route model/gpt-4-small --prefer tcp --reason "fabric packet loss"
```

alex: drain started, pods are rescheduling to node-09/10. rdctl returned OK for prefer=tcp.

pagerbot: :white_check_mark: rdctl config change approved by infra policy. Change id cfg-7723.

support-lead: Customer impact so far? any high-priority customers affected?

maria: short term: ~12% increase in 5xx for inference tier in us-west-2 over last 10m. Tail latency increased to 5-10s for some requests. No complete outage, but degraded. A handful of enterprise customers (acct-231, acct-522) reported increased retries.

support-lead: logging ticket updates now and enabling SLO alerting for those accounts.

chen: monitoring shows retransmit rate jumped at 14:22:11 UTC from baseline 0.3% to 7.8% on sw-rack7 port-3. I ran iperf between node-07 and node-09, observed packet loss and reordering.

alex: I've also lowered route batch_size from 64->16 and max_concurrency 8->2 for the affected model via feature flag. This should reduce per-pod memory pressure.

```json
{"route":"model/gpt-4-small","batch_size":16,"max_concurrency":2,"feature_flag":"emergency_mem_limit"}
```

maria: after drain + tcp fallback + batch changes, pods restarted and CV (cache) warmups look normal. Error rate trending down.

chen: infra is engaging the fabric team. We're seeing a suspected transient firmware bug causing packet reordering on that switch port. We'll keep cordoned nodes offline until switch patch or traffic shift.

alex: status update for handoff: cordoned node-06/07, tcp-fallback enabled for model/gpt-4-small, batch_size reduced, scaling up extra tcp-only replicas in us-west-2 + draining in progress. customer impact: degraded latency and increased 5xx for 10-15m window, now improving.

ryan: taking over for next 2 hours. summary ok. action items for me:
- keep nodes cordoned until fabric team confirms fix
- monitor CUDA OOM regressions for next 1h
- rollback batch size only once stable for 30m
- update incident channel and runbook link

alex: noted. leaving logs and commands above. handing off to @ryan.

ryan: thanks. I'm patching runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/fabric-degradation

sre-bot: :information_source: Incident status changed -> Mitigated (partial). Follow-up required: fabric firmware ticket TF-4498, ISP switch replacement scheduled.

support-lead: I'll send customer comms template and post updates to affected accounts.

maria: monitoring shows error rate at baseline after 18m. memory usage per pod stable.

ryan: I'll keep the cordon for 2 hours and then test reintroducing node-07 with no traffic.

alex: thanks all. filing postmortem stub and linking telemetry.

sre-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident closed to on-call. If regression happens re-open with same thread.
